title: Noise-decoupled SLO attribution and graduated paging
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Reduce noisy pages and improve SLO attribution accuracy by separating transient noise from actionable degradations. This work refactors trace hooks to emit lightweight cohort hints, enriches metrics/log pipelines with session and model_variant keys, and implements a graduated paging policy that uses anomaly confidence to decide escalation windows.
acceptance_criteria: Trace-hook adapter implemented and deployed to prod sidecars with <5% CPU overhead
Key SLOs (request P99 latency, generation error rate) accurately attributed to a single service/cohort >=85% of the time in postmortem validations
New graduated paging policy reduces pages from known noise sources by >=40% compared to baseline in a 2-week A/B
Auditable dashboards for cohort-level latency and error slices plus an anomaly-confidence metric visible in Console
Rollout plan with canary, kill-switch, and runbook updates published
tasks: Design: define cohort keys (route, model_variant, sequence_length_bucket)
Engineering: refactor trace-hook API to attach sampling_hint and cohort_tags
Pipeline: add enrichment stage in metrics/logs pipeline to surface cohort_tags
Anomaly: train lightweight confidence scorer using recent baseline windows
Console: build cohort heatmap and anomaly-confidence chart for SLO dashboard
Policy: implement graduated paging agent using confidence thresholds and quiet-hours rules
Testing: synthetic degradation runs and 2-week A/B with existing pager policy
Docs: update runbooks and oncall playbooks with new suppression and escalation logic
implementation_notes: Trace-hook refactor must be backward compatible: older sidecars should still emit existing span attributes when new flags are off
Sampling_hint is a 1-byte enum (0=none,1=rare,2=default,3=high) to guide adaptive trace sampling downstream
Cohort tags are a short key:value set (max 3 tags) to avoid cardinality explosion in metrics
Enrichment stage will run in the pipeline worker pool with a small in-memory cache for recent mapping rules
Anomaly confidence uses a small gradient-boosted model with features: recent p50/p95/p99 deltas, error spike ratio, request volume drop
Graduated paging uses thresholds: confidence>0.9 -> page primary, 0.7-0.9 -> page on-call with 10m delay, 0.5-0.7 -> paging suppressed but create incident ticket
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: increased cardinality from cohort tags -> mitigate by restricting to fixed buckets and sampling_reporting
Risk: false suppression causing missed outages -> keep conservative thresholds during canary and enable automatic fallback to old policy
Risk: model drift in anomaly scorer -> schedule weekly retraining job and surface feature drift metrics
Risk: sidecar overhead -> benchmark at 0.5% RPS sample and tune sampling_hint defaults
deployment_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable trace-hook adapter and pipeline enrichment for 5% of traffic to obs-test org
Phase 2 (staged): expand to 30% and run synthetic degradation harness to validate attribution
Phase 3 (rollout): enable graduated paging with conservative thresholds for 14 days
Phase 4 (tune): adjust thresholds after A/B and flip to aggressive thresholds if safety checks pass
notes: Spike experiments showed cohort grouping by model_variant+route reduced attribution ambiguity for cache-miss storms
Oncall asked for a 10-minute delayed escalation option for medium-confidence anomalies to reduce noisy wakeups
Coordination required with Platform Infra for pipeline worker quota increases during canary
